history.text: before we build anything i want to pin down how outgoing webhooks work for customers. push every event to one url, or subscriptions per event type?

Per-event-type subscriptions are the usual choice: customers only receive what they handle, and new event types surprise nobody. Pushing everything is simpler to build but noisy, and every customer ends up filtering on their side. I'd go with subscriptions, each with its own signing secret.
what about retries when their endpoint is down?
Exponential backoff for about a day, then mark the subscription as failing and notify the account owner. Delivery stays at-least-once, so every payload carries an id for de-duplication.
how do we version the payloads then?
Pin a payload version per subscription when it is created; new versions ship side by side and customers upgrade one subscription at a time.
and ordering?
Don't promise global ordering. Include a per-resource sequence number and a timestamp so consumers can discard stale updates.
